refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement asserts contractible-fibre weak equivalences for every X and N. Take X to be a point and N=R. Imm(X,R)=R, while Imm(X×[0,1],R) has increasing and decreasing components. Restriction evaluates at 0, and each fibre has both components, so it is not contractible and the map is not a weak homotopy equivalence. Proof 1.1 incorrectly identifies that fibre with paths in Imm(X,R).

The genuine-immersion clause fails for X=[-1,1], A=[-1,-1/2]∪[1/2,1], N=R. Start with the identity and move the left component by +2t and the right by −2t. This is a path of immersions on A, but at t=1 the left interval maps to the right of the right interval. Any extension through immersions of connected X into R must remain increasing, so the path has no lift.

The Statement omits ACω, while its [L1] dependency, thm-smale-hirsch-for-open-source-manifolds, explicitly begins “Assume the axiom of countable choice”; its metric supplier thm-every-smooth-vector-bundle-admits-a-smooth-bundle-metric also explicitly assumes ACω. The statement does not make this required premise clear.

The Statement calls Immν(M,N) a subspace of Imm(M,N) consisting of immersions whose normal bundle is “identified with νF.” But def-space-of-immersions-and-space-of-formal-immersions defines Imm(M,N) as a space of maps; a chosen normal-bundle isomorphism is extra data, not represented in that subspace. If interpreted as mere isomorphism type, take M=point, N=R: the target is R, while Imm(D¹,R) has two monotonicity components, so restriction cannot be a weak homotopy equivalence.

The cited in-scope dependency lem-formal-immersion-homotopies-extend-over-a-collar concerns restrictions Imm(X×[0,1],N)→Imm(X,N) and FImm(X×[0,1],N)→FImm(X,N); it does not state a transfer from int D(νF) to D(νF). Its claimed product restriction is itself false for X=point, N=R. Thus [L2] does not license Proof 3.1’s transfer from the interior to the closed disk bundle.

The proof states “A map with contractible fibres is a weak homotopy equivalence” without establishing a fibration or a continuous fibrewise contraction. This implication is false in general: projection from the closed topologist’s sine curve onto [0,1] is surjective with contractible fibres but has two path components in its domain and one in its target.

The proof asserts that TD(νF) splits as π*TM⊕π*νF “along the horizontal and vertical directions,” but [F1] supplies only the tangent-normal splitting of (f∘π)*TN. A connection or another construction of the horizontal splitting is needed. This is a short, standard step to supply, so the gap is nonfatal.

reader_findings.evidence: The proof identifies Imm(X×I,N) with paths in Imm(X,N). A smooth family is only slice-wise immersive; its derivative in the I direction need not be independent of the X derivatives. Take X=[0,1], N=R: Imm(X,R) is nonempty, but Imm(X×I,R) is empty by dimensions, so restriction cannot be a weak equivalence. Even for X a point and N=R, the fibre of Imm(I,R)→R has increasing and decreasing components. The opened def-compact-parameter-pair and smoothing lemma supply families, not immersions of the full product. Replace this with a collar extension of unchanged source dimension and prove the actual restriction homotopy equivalence; adding a target-dimension bound alone does not make the fibres contractible.

reader_findings.location: Statement, analogous restriction on genuine immersions; Proof 4.1
reader_findings.evidence: The unrestricted genuine-immersion Serre-fibration assertion is false. Let X=[-1,1], A=[-1,-1/2]⊔[1/2,1], N=R, with initial immersion the identity. On the left component set g_t(x)=x+2t and on the right set g_t(x)=x−2t. Every g_t is an immersion of A, but the endpoint reverses the order of the two images and cannot extend to a monotone immersion of X continuing the identity. Formal bundle monomorphisms can be perturbed linearly; genuine derivatives cannot be treated as arbitrary such sections. Francis, Lectures 5–6, p.1, Lemma 1.3 and Note 1.4 impose n>k and give the endpoint-swap obstruction. Remove or correctly restrict the genuine clause and prove its lifting statement with the required dimension hypotheses.

reader_findings.location: Statement (ii), definition of Imm_ν and FImm_ν as subspaces
reader_findings.evidence: Normal-bundle identification is additional data, not a property defining a subspace of the unframed immersion space. Francis, Lectures 5–6, p.3, Definition 1.8 uses pairs consisting of an immersion and a specified normal-bundle isomorphism; p.4 then uses the forgetful fibre bundles. As unframed subspaces, (ii) is false for M a point and N=R: Imm(D^1,R) has two orientation components whereas Imm(point,R)=R is contractible. Define the spaces of pairs and their topologies, retain the identification in restriction, and prove the corresponding forgetful-fibration comparison.

F1 supplies the disk-bundle manifold and the zero-section tangent-normal splitting, not a global horizontal splitting TD(ν)≅π*TM⊕π*ν; a connection or a proved splitting of the vertical tangent exact sequence is missing. Step 2.1 gives no explicit fibre contraction or fibration/homotopy-inverse argument; contractible fibres alone do not imply weak equivalence for an arbitrary map. Its cited Euclidean tubular results do not establish the extension into arbitrary N without the metric/exponential construction. Step 3.1 also relies on the false product-collar lemma. State AC_ω for the metric and open-source suppliers, prove the horizontal splitting and parametric exponential/shrinking construction, and replace the collar transfer. Francis Lemma 1.9, p.3, and the framed forgetful-fibration argument on p.4 identify the intended route but do not license the current shortcuts.

reader_findings.location: Historical observation: Statement and Facts L2; Proof 3.1–4.1
reader_findings.evidence: The observed statement asserted splitting for every formal immersion without a choice premise, while L2 invoked the published smooth-complement and smooth-metric suppliers, both explicitly assuming AC_ω. That prerequisite was not stated. The producer has since added Assume AC_ω to the current statement. This is a retained historical observation, not a claim that the corrected bytes contain the omission. The original raw source hash was not recorded, so observed_source is null.

The observed definition concluded necessarily m≤n from pointwise injectivity without excluding an empty source. For the empty m-manifold the fibre condition is vacuous, even when m>n. The producer has since qualified the inequality by when M is nonempty and explicitly handled the empty pair. No old raw hash was captured; this historical evidence is retained with observed_source null and does not allege a defect in the corrected current definition.

reader_findings.location: Historical observation: Statement general bundle clause; Proof 3.1
reader_findings.evidence: The observed general clause allowed a rank-r bundle over an s-dimensional closed manifold with merely a finite zero set, then wrote ⟨w_r(E),[S]⟩ as a scalar. This evaluation requires r=s; for r≠s, transversality can give an empty, hence finite, zero set while the displayed pairing still has mismatched degrees. The producer has since restricted the scalar count clause to an r-dimensional base and corrected the homology pushforward. The original raw bytes were not hashed when read; observed_source is null and this is historical, not a current-byte allegation.

reader_findings.location: Historical observation: Statement, ν_Z≅s*E|_Z and final equivalently evaluation clause
reader_findings.evidence: The observed statement used s*E although s:M→E is a section rather than a map to the base of the bundle E→M; the normal identification is with E|_Z. It also equated nonzero zero-locus homology with a scalar evaluation ⟨e(E),[M]⟩ for arbitrary r,n, which is undefined when r≠n and can cancel on disconnected bases when r=n. The producer has since corrected both statements and the numerical caveat. The earlier raw source hash was not captured, so observed_source is null; the observation is retained historically and is not asserted of the corrected bytes.
